newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Steady Fed fails to cheer U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Steady Fed fails to cheer U.S. markets.

text.p: U.S. stocks edged into narrowly positive territory, but bonds sagged in tandem with a battered dollar after the Federal Reserve's decision to hold U.S. interest rates steady on Tuesday.

Wall Street analysts had been sharply divided over whether the Fed would hike rates or leave them unchanged, keeping financial markets unusually jittery in the hours preceding the Federal Open Market Committee's decision.
Both bonds and stocks popped higher after the Fed meeting ended with no change in rates, but gains proved short-lived.

"I think the real issue is a question of timing," said Charles Lieberman, director of financial markets research at Chase Securities Inc. "I expected the Fed to leave policy unchanged today but I think rates are going to end up higher."
Data released late last month showed the economy grew at a 5.6 percent annualized clip in the first quarter of 1997 -- its fastest rate in more than nine years.

And with the unemployment rate at its lowest point in almost 24 years, some analysts fear that it is only a matter of time before workers begin demanding the higher wages that will ultimately lead to higher inflation.
